name: Constant-α Monte Carlo

symbols.meaning: the actual return after time t

intuition: Monte Carlo with a fixed step: the target is the whole return, known only when the episode ends.
pitfalls: The update cannot be made until the episode is over.

name: TD(0) update
intuition: Learn a guess from a guess: one sampled step plus the current estimate of where it led.
pitfalls: The target uses the current estimate $V(S_{t+1})$, not the true $v_\pi(S_{t+1})$.

name: The value as an expected return (the Monte Carlo target)
tex: v_\pi(s) = \mathbb{E}_\pi[G_t \mid S_t = s] = \mathbb{E}_\pi\Big[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \gamma^k R_{t+k+1} \,\Big|\, S_t = s\Big]
intuition: A state's value is the average return from it. Monte Carlo estimates this expectation by sampled returns.
assumptions: The value definition of Chapter 3; the printed (6.3) is the first line of a chain that ends at (6.4).
pitfalls: The Monte Carlo target is an estimate only because it samples: it uses no other estimate.

name: The value through its successor (the DP target)
tex: v_\pi(s) = \mathbb{E}_\pi\Big[R_{t+1} + \gamma \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \gamma^k R_{t+k+2} \,\Big|\, S_t = s\Big] = \mathbb{E}_\pi\big[R_{t+1} + \gamma v_\pi(S_{t+1}) \mid S_t = s\big]

symbols.meaning: the value of the next state, standing for all later rewards

intuition: Split off the first reward; the rest of the return is, in expectation, the value of the next state.

derivation.why: Take the k = 0 term out of the sum and shift the index.
The remaining sum is the return from time t + 1, whose expectation given the next state is that state's value.

significance: DP uses (6.4) with the expectation computed from a model and the current estimate V in place of $v_\pi$. TD(0) uses it with the expectation sampled and V in place of $v_\pi$: both kinds of estimate at once.
pitfalls: The DP target is an estimate because of V, not because of the expectation, which the model gives exactly.

name: Sarsa update

symbols.meaning: the next action actually chosen by the (ε-greedy) policy

intuition: The target uses the action the agent will really take next, so exploration is part of what is learned.
pitfalls: $A_{t+1}$ must be chosen before the update and then actually taken.

name: Q-learning update

symbols.meaning: the value of the best next action, whatever the agent does next

intuition: The target assumes the best action from the next state, so Q learns the optimal values while the agent explores.
assumptions: All state–action pairs must keep being updated for convergence to $q_*$ (p. 157).
pitfalls: The next action taken may differ from the one in the target; that is what makes Q-learning off-policy.
